title: Expansion planning hold lifecycle
description: Objective: define the pure core lifecycle for a runner-safe expansion request and its exact EXPANSION_PLANNING hold. Deliverable: a frozen reducer/contract that binds the resumable parent, worker handoff, planning run, proposal base, graph epoch, source fingerprint, deadline, and terminal cause, without minting children or execution authority. NOT in scope: PlanningRun submission, scheduler admission, resource/budget preparation, graph approval/activation, persistence, or daemon commands. Owned paths: packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-planning-hold.ts, expansion-planning-hold.js, expansion-planning-hold.test.ts. Production consumers: the Planning-run expansion submission child and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: A closed immutable hold contract and reducer admit a request only at a supplied runner-proven safe release boundary and bind exact parent node/run, worker handoff, planning run, proposal base, graph epoch, source fingerprint, deadline, and generation.

The only lifecycle is ACTIVE to RESOLVED, SUPERSEDED, or CANCELLED; duplicate commands replay byte-identically, stale generation/version or mismatched binding refuses with exact stable code and layer, and no terminal state can reactivate.
Every accepted/refused result is deeply frozen and contains no child run, lease, effect, slot, resource, budget-allocation, graph-activation, or command authority.

Focused transition/race/hostile-input tests assert exact code plus layer, unchanged state on refusal, nonzero generated-case counts, deterministic replay, and a production-guard mutation that turns the suite red.
The exact verification command exits 0, production files remain below 400 lines, and both named consumer tasks are recorded.
taskRails: A request may record AGENT_REPORTED rationale but it never upgrades the safe-boundary or dependency truth.
Do not duplicate PlanningRun, graph revision, budget, or daemon persistence authority in this reducer.
No automatic approval or child activation affordance.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected importing @moe/runner or @moe/scheduler: @moe/core depends only on @moe/contracts and must consume exact projected receipt references rather than fork release authority. Rejected createRuntimeError for hold concurrency/lifecycle refusals: the committed runtime registry does not allow PLANNING_HOLD as the source for EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, or ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, so those calls would degrade to UNKNOWN_ERROR. Use a closed domain-local code/layer union instead. Rejected omitting the required .js bridge or deferring publication: core's runtime-entrypoint.test.ts marks every bridge not reachable from src/index.ts as unexpected; the narrow src/index.ts amendment is therefore required now. Rejected embedding the hold in PlanningRun: the design makes PlanningHold a first-class aggregate/readiness predicate and the next child owns PlanningRun composition.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Design SHA-256 was reverified. Design lines 238/455 require an exact EXPANSION_PLANNING hold bound to one affected parent, one PlanningRun, proposal base, graph epoch, source fingerprint, deadline and ACTIVE->RESOLVED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED lifecycle. The request is legal only after a runner-proven WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE boundary with attempt/lease/provider slot released, effects/resources terminal and exact handoff; rationale remains AGENT_REPORTED. @moe/contracts already freezes PLANNING_HOLD lifecycle/kind and truth vocabularies. Existing core hostile-input helpers show the required exact-key/snapshot/deep-freeze pattern, but this focused module must remain self-contained inside its owned leaf. Runtime command replay normally belongs to the decision ledger; this two-transition aggregate additionally keeps bounded creation/terminal receipts so the immediately or historically repeated creation/terminal command can reconstruct byte-identical original state/event results, while same commandId with changed bytes refuses. packages/core/src/index.ts is clean and 221 lines; explicit curated expansion exports can remain under 250. Consumers are task-fcad40b6d26243439cd19fd3e49c924d and durable daemon task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2.
planningNotes.risks: Do not treat a caller boolean as release proof: require exact receipt refs, the closed WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE/RELEASED/resumable facts and DAEMON_VERIFIED truth, leaving authoritative sourcing to the daemon consumer. Deadline is immutable evidence only and must never auto-clear a hold. A cancel/decline/refusal with live, unknown or missing terminal authority proof leaves ACTIVE unchanged. Same-ID changed payload must be distinguished from a true replay before stale-version checks. Preserve original handoff/bindings in every terminal state so parent resume is exact. Terminal states never reactivate. No Date.now, randomness, crypto, IO, child authority, or imported runner/scheduler code. Keep expansion-planning-hold.ts target <=250 and strictly <400; keep src/index.ts <=250 and explicitly curated to avoid export collisions.
